Modern Japanese anime style, clean crisp cel shading, Makoto Shinkai-inspired atmospheric lighting, cinematic wide shot, highly detailed. The same young woman field ecologist with a short dark-blue bob haircut and olive green field vest over a white shirt stands on a grassy ridge at golden hour, repeatedly scanning the landscape with a large handheld sensor device. Behind and beside her are four semi-transparent ghost-like duplicates of her in successive positions, each scanning, forming a rhythmic sequence that reads as repeated survey effort. All of the duplicates project cyan scanning beams that travel a long way across the valley and then get visibly clipped, terminating at a horizontal glowing amber barrier of light floating at a fixed low altitude. Above the amber barrier, two tiny identical bird silhouettes remain permanently unresolved, never getting closer, never changing. The amber light barrier is clearly a hard floor that the beams cannot pass through no matter how many times she scans. Warm amber barrier glow, cool cyan beams, layered depth.
